about: Setup notes for MCP clients, rendered on the Connect page. Data only: the gateway has no client-specific code. 'documented' means the steps come from the client's own documentation on the checked date; no entry is a recorded live connection. 'unverified' means the documentation leaves part of the flow unclear. Product menus move; the server URL and 'sign in when asked' are what stay true.

clients.name: ChatGPT
steps: Add a custom MCP server. Current layouts: Plugins, then Add custom MCP server. Older workspace layouts: Settings, Apps, Create (developer mode).
Paste the server address and choose OAuth.
Leave the OAuth client ID and secret empty.
Create it, then sign in and approve when asked.
clients.note: ChatGPT takes no API key. Your plan and workspace decide whether custom servers are available.

clients.name: Claude.ai and Claude Desktop
steps: Open Customize, then Connectors, then Add custom connector. On Team and Enterprise plans an owner adds it under Organization settings, Connectors first.
Paste the server address. Leave the advanced OAuth client ID and secret empty and add no request headers.
Select Connect, sign in and approve.
clients.note: Each person connects with their own sign-in, so each gets their own plan.

clients.name: Claude Code
steps: Run: claude mcp add --transport http azizam <server address>
Run /mcp in Claude Code and choose Authenticate to sign in.
Or use an app key: add --header "Authorization: Bearer <your app key>".

clients.name: Cursor
steps: Add the server to mcp.json: {"mcpServers": {"azizam": {"url": "<server address>"}}}
Cursor asks you to sign in the first time it connects.
Or use an app key: add "headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer <your app key>"}.

clients.name: VS Code
steps: Run MCP: Add Server, choose HTTP and paste the server address.
VS Code asks you to sign in and approve.
Or use an app key through a headers entry with an input variable.

clients.name: Windsurf (Cascade)
steps: Add a server with "serverUrl": "<server address>" to the MCP configuration.
Sign in when asked, or add an Authorization header with your app key.
clients.note: The documentation does not say which sign-in method Windsurf uses.

clients.name: Goose
steps: Run goose configure, then Add Extension, then Remote Extension (Streamable HTTP).
Paste the server address. Goose opens a browser to sign in.
Or add the header Authorization: Bearer <your app key>.

clients.name: Zed
steps: Add a context server with "url": "<server address>" in Zed's settings.
Without an Authorization header Zed signs in through the browser; with one it uses your app key.
clients.note: The documentation does not say which protocol versions Zed sends.

clients.name: LibreChat
steps: In librechat.yaml under mcpServers add: type: streamable-http and url: <server address>. Set the type: without it LibreChat uses the old SSE transport.
Each user signs in from LibreChat when first using the server.
Or set headers with Authorization: Bearer and requiresOAuth: false.

clients.name: Open WebUI
steps: An admin adds an MCP (Streamable HTTP) tool server with the server address.
Choose OAuth 2.1 (dynamic registration) so each user signs in, or Bearer with an app key.
Do not choose the OAuth or Session modes: they send Open WebUI's own sign-in, which this server refuses.

clients.name: MCP Inspector
steps: Run: npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector
Choose Streamable HTTP, paste the server address and connect. Use the OAuth flow to sign in, or add an Authorization header.
